sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Ajit Ku. Agrawal - Advocate for the appellant.
 None for the respondents - though served.

Order 
The issue involved in this misc. appeal is limited as appellant - Insurance Company is assailing the award passed on 28.08.2014 by First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raisen (for short 'the Tribunal') in Claim Case No.83/2013 on the ground for the breach of insurance policy appellant - Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation amount.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The facts of the accident are not in dispute hence they are not being discussed here.
The learned Tribunal allowed the claim petition for Rs.19,00,000/- and held that appellant - Insurance Company jointly and severely liable to honour the award.

The Tribunal relying on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of S.Iyyapan Vs. M/S United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & Another,
2013(3) ACCD 1337 (Supreme Court) held that if the driver was having a driving licence regarding light motor vehicle and was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18363 2 MA-2685-2014 driving a commercial vehicle even then the Insurance Company shall be liable to pay compensation under the principle of pay and recover.

entities.text:

2013(3) ACCD 1337 (Supreme Court)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This finding has been assailed in the present appeal and appellant - Insurance Company is claiming complete exoneration from its liability.
3. Arguments of learned counsel for appellant have been heard and the record has been perused.

sentences.text: 4. The Hon'ble Apex Court after considering the conflicting decisions on the issue whether a person holding a driving licence to drive a light motor vehicle can also drive a transport vehicle having a weight of not more than 7500 Kgs., held in Mukund Devangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2017) 14 SCC 663 that no separate endorsement on licnece was required under the amendment incorporated in Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and a driver holding a license to drive a light motor vehicle can also drive a transport vehicle of similar class without obtaining endorsement on his driving licence.

entities.text: Mukund Devangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This decision has reiterated what was held by the Apex Court in the case of New India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Dujiya Bai and others, 2007 JLJ 319.
5.

entities.text: New India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Dujiya Bai and others, 2007 JLJ 319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In terms of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court settling the conflicting views, no contention can now be legally entertained about complete exoneration of Insurance Company from the liability for breach of insurance policy for not having an endorsement of transport vehicle on the driving license provided that he was duly licensed to drive a light motor vehicle of similar class.

Incidentally,
the gross weight of offending vehicle in this case was only 850 Kgs.
In the light of the well settled legal proposition, this appeal preferred by the appellant - Insurance Company for complete exoneration from liability fails and is, accordingly, dismissed.
7. Record be sent back to the Tribunal along with the copy of this order.
